title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON SPECIAL MEASURES FOR RESTORATION REGISTRATION AND PRESERVATION REGISTRATION OF LAND WITH UNRESTORED OWNERSHIP REGISTRATION IN RECOVERED AREAS
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to provide for matters delegated by the Act on Special Measures for Restoration Registration and Preservation Registration of Land with Unrestored Ownership Registration in Recovered Areas (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 Deleted. <Dec. 31, 1988>

CHAPTER II REGISTRATION OF RESTORATION OF OWNERSHIP

Article 3 (Application for registration of restoration of ownership) (1) An application for the registration of restoration of ownership under Article 4(1) of the Act shall be made in Form 1.
  (2) The document evidencing ownership under Article 4(1) of the Act shall be the applicable one among the following documents:
  1. A certified copy of the land (forest land) ledger;
  2. A certified copy or abstract of the real estate register, or a document evidencing registration;
  3. A written judgment of a court relating to ownership.
  (3) Where the applicant for the registration of restoration of ownership is an heir, he or she shall attach, in addition to the applicable document under the subparagraphs of paragraph (2), a document evidencing the fact of inheritance.

Article 4 (Qualifications of guarantors) (1) Grounds for disqualification of a guarantor under Article 5(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. An incompetent or quasi-incompetent person;
  2. A person declared bankrupt and not yet reinstated;
  3. A person for whom 3 years have not elapsed since the execution of a sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment was completed or the non-execution of such sentence became final;
  4. A person who is under a stay of execution of a sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment and the period of stay has not expired;
  5. A person who is under a stay of sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment.
  (2) Where the head of a Si/Gun determines the scope of neighboring Ri/Dong pursuant to the latter part of Article 5(1) of the Act, the criteria therefor shall be within the scope of the Si/Gun to which the Ri/Dong where the relevant land is located belongs and the Si/Gun adjacent thereto.

Article 5 (Appointment and dismissal of guarantors) (1) When the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon appoints a guarantor pursuant to Article 5(2) of the Act, such appointment shall be made upon the recommendation of the head of the Ri/Dong where the land is located if residents reside there at all times, or upon the recommendation of the head of a neighboring Ri/Dong determined and publicly notified by the competent head of a Si/Gun pursuant to the latter part of Article 5(1) of the Act if residents do not reside in the Ri/Dong where the land is located at all times. In such cases, the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon shall submit relevant documents in advance to the Land Owner Restoration Examination Committee having jurisdiction over the relevant land to undergo an examination regarding the qualifications of the guarantor.
  (2) The head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon shall appoint no fewer than 3 but no more than 5 guarantors for each Ri/Dong where the land is located and shall publicly announce such appointment and the personal particulars of the guarantors.
  (3) When a guarantor appointed under paragraph (2) is unable to perform his or her duties, he or she shall, without delay, notify the head of the relevant Si/Gun or Eup/Myeon of the grounds therefor.
  (4) When the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon deems that a guarantor has violated the provisions of Article 6 or that it is inappropriate to continue to have him or her as a guarantor, or upon receipt of a notification of grounds for inability to perform duties under paragraph (3), he or she shall dismiss the relevant guarantor without delay and appoint a new guarantor.
  (5) The recommendation, appointment, and dismissal of guarantors shall be made in Forms 2 through 4, respectively.

Article 6 (Duties of guarantors) (1) A guarantor shall perform his or her duties independently, fairly, faithfully, and promptly, and shall not have another person perform such duties on his or her behalf.
  (2) A guarantor shall not receive any remuneration, gift, or entertainment in connection with his or her duties.

Article 7 (Maintenance of register of appointed guarantors and affixing of seals) (1) When the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon appoints a guarantor pursuant to Article 5(2), he or she shall prepare and maintain a register of appointed guarantors in Form 5.
  (2) A guarantor shall, within 3 days from the date of appointment, appear before the competent authority or the Eup/Myeon office of the location of the land, report the seal to be used for preparing written guarantees, and affix the seal to the register of appointed guarantors under paragraph (1).
  (3) When the head of an Eup/Myeon receives a report of a guarantor's seal pursuant to paragraph (2), he or she shall submit 1 copy of the register of appointed guarantors under paragraph (1) to the competent head of a Gun.

Article 8 (Procedures for issuance of written guarantees) (1) A person who intends to obtain a written guarantee under Article 4(2) of the Act shall obtain guarantees from not fewer than 3 guarantors appointed pursuant to Article 5(2) and file an application for issuance of a written guarantee with a guarantor designated pursuant to paragraph (3).
  (2) Where an application is filed under paragraph (1), the guarantor designated pursuant to paragraph (3) shall, where guarantees from not fewer than 3 guarantors have been obtained, without delay issue a written guarantee in Form 6 by assigning a serial number thereto, enter such issuance in the register of issuance of written guarantees in Form 7, and obtain the seal of the applicant thereon. In such cases, where a guarantor other than those who have affixed their seals to the written guarantee raises an objection to the application, the grounds therefor shall be stated in the register of issuance of written guarantees.
  (3) The register of issuance of written guarantees under paragraph (1) shall be prepared and maintained by a person designated by the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon from among the guarantors of the relevant Ri/Dong.

Article 9 (Public announcement) (1) A public announcement under Article 8(1) of the Act shall specify the purpose of the announcement, description of the land, name, address, and resident registration number of the applicant, grounds for acquisition, period of announcement, procedures for filing objections, and other necessary matters, and shall be made in Form 8; provided, if such announcement is published in a daily newspaper, only the purpose of the announcement, the location and lot number among the description of the land, the period of announcement, procedures for filing objections, and other necessary matters may be specified. <Amended on Mar. 16, 1984>
  (2) The competent authority shall make a public announcement within 1 month from the date of receipt of an application for the registration of restoration of ownership.
  (3) A public announcement posted on the bulletin board of the offices of a Si/Gun, etc. pursuant to Article 8(1) of the Act shall be continuously posted until the expiration of the period of public announcement under that paragraph.
  (4) Any person who has an objection to the details of a public announcement under paragraph (1) may file an objection with the competent authority in Form 9 by the expiration date of the period of public announcement.

Article 10 (Referral of applications for registration of restoration of ownership to examination) When documents are referred to a Si/Gun Land Owner Restoration Examination Committee (hereinafter referred to as "Si/Gun Committee") pursuant to Article 8(2) of the Act, matters necessary for preparing a written decision on examination for the registration of restoration of land ownership in Form 10 shall be stated for each application and attached as a cover sheet.

Article 11 (Examination by Si/Gun Committee) (1) Where an application for the registration of restoration of ownership, an objection, or other relevant documents are referred for examination pursuant to Article 10, the Si/Gun Committee shall, in principle, conduct its examination based on documents; provided, when it is deemed impracticable to determine the true owner based solely on documents, it may conduct a fact-finding investigation for examination.
  (2) Records of fact-finding investigations under paragraph (1) shall be compiled with the relevant documents and preserved.

Article 12 (Decision on examination by Si/Gun Committee) (1) A written decision under Article 10(1) of the Act shall be in Form 10.
  (2) Service of a certified copy of the written decision under Article 10(3) of the Act shall be effected by personal service or by registered mail, and a register of service of written decisions on examination of restoration registration of land ownership shall be prepared and maintained in Form 11. In such cases, the certified copy of the written decision served upon the competent authority shall be accompanied by the entire set of documents referred by the competent authority to the committee.

Article 13 (Request for re-examination) (1) A request for re-examination under Article 11(1) of the Act shall be made by submitting a written request for re-examination in Form 12, along with relevant evidentiary documents, to the competent authority.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for re-examination under paragraph (1), the competent authority shall, within 10 days, transmit the request to the Land Owner Restoration Re-examination Committee (hereinafter referred to as "Do Committee"), along with a written explanation, a copy of the written decision, and other necessary documents.
  (3) Where the Do Committee that has received a request for re-examination is unable to conduct a re-examination due to a defect in the written request or the insufficiency of evidentiary documents to prove the grounds for dissatisfaction, it shall return the request to the applicant while specifying a period for supplementation. In such cases, if the written request for re-examination is not re-submitted within the period for supplementation, the request for re-examination shall be deemed withdrawn.
  (4) In calculating the periods under Article 11(1) and (2) of the Act, the calculation shall be based on the date on which the competent authority receives the request for re-examination.

Article 14 (Registration of restoration of ownership) Where the competent authority having jurisdiction restores and registers an owner pursuant to Article 12(3) of the Act, it shall state the grounds for the registration of restoration of ownership in the land ledger or forest land ledger.

CHAPTER III LAND OWNER RESTORATION EXAMINATION COMMITTEE

Article 15 (Duties of chairperson) (1) The chairperson of each committee shall represent the committee and shall oversee its business affairs. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to an accident, the vice-chairperson shall act on his or her behalf; and where both the chairperson and the vice-chairperson are unable to perform their duties due to an accident, a member designated by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf.

Article 16 (Meetings of committee) (1) Meetings of each committee shall be convened by the chairperson.
  (2) When the chairperson convenes a meeting of the committee, he or she shall notify each member in writing of the date, time, place, and agenda of the meeting at least 5 days prior to the meeting; provided, this shall not apply to cases where urgent or unavoidable circumstances exist. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (3) A meeting of each committee shall open with the attendance of at least 2/3 of the members on the current registry, including the chairperson, and shall resolve by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
  (4) Allowances and travel expenses for on-site fact-finding investigations may be paid, within the budgetary limit, to members attending meetings of each committee; provided, no allowances shall be paid to members who are public officials.
  (5) Each committee shall prepare and maintain minutes of meetings.

Article 17 (Appointment and dismissal of members) (1) The appointment of a member shall be made in Form 13.
  (2) When a member under Article 7(2)5 and Article 7(3)4 of the Act falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun shall dismiss the relevant member without delay and appoint a new member: in such cases, the dismissal of a member shall be made in Form 14:
  1. Where a member dies;
  2. Where a member is unable to perform his or her duties due to illness or is deemed otherwise inappropriate.

Article 18 (Secretary) (1) One secretary shall be appointed to handle the business affairs of each committee.
  The competent authority shall, with respect to land with unrestored ownership registration to be acquired as State property pursuant to Article 20 of the Act, prepare a land inventory as of the expiration date of the effective period of the Act (or, in cases under the proviso to Addenda 2 of the Act, the date of the decision or decision on re-examination by the relevant committee), and submit it to the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended on Dec. 23, 1994>

CHAPTER IV REGISTRATION OF CHANGE IN NAME OF OWNER AND REPORT OF CADASTRAL MOVEMENT

Article 19 (Registration of change in name of owner) (1) A person who intends to apply for registration of a change in the name of the owner under Article 13(1) of the Act shall submit a written application in Form 15, along with a certificate issued under Article 19 of the Act, to the competent authority in the case of land, or to the head of a Si or the head of an Eup/Myeon in the case of a building.
  (2) When the competent authority or the head of a Si, Eup, or Myeon registers a change in the name of the owner under Article 13(2) of the Act, it shall state the grounds for such change in the ownership change column of the land ledger, forest land ledger, or building ledger without delay.

Article 20 (Application for cadastral movement) (1) An application for change in land particulars in the cadastral records under Article 14(1) of the Act shall be made in Form 16, and an application for change in building indications shall be made in Form 17.
  (2) Where a person intends to apply for correction of any error in the registered particulars of the cadastral records under Article 14(3) of the Act, such application shall be made in Form 18.

Article 21 (Issuance of certified copies of ledgers) Where the registration of restoration of ownership is made pursuant to Article 14 or registration of a change in the name of the owner is made pursuant to Article 19, and a request for a certified copy of the ledger is made within 3 months, the competent authority shall issue the certified copy of the ledger with a statement in the margin that an application for the registration of preservation of ownership may be filed based on the certified copy of the ledger after 3 months have elapsed from the date of the restoration registration or change of registration pursuant to Article 15(1) of the Act.

Article 22 (Issuance of certificate of facts for vested property) The certificate of facts issued by the head of a tax office pursuant to Article 17(1) of the Act shall be in Form 19.

Article 23 (Application for issuance of certificates) (1) An application for issuance of a certificate under Article 19(1) of the Act shall be made in Form 20.
  (2) Regarding the issuance of a written guarantee to be attached to a certificate under Article 19(2) of the Act, Article 8 shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 24 (Public announcement) (1) A public announcement under Article 19(3) of the Act shall specify the purpose of the announcement, description of the real estate, the registered owner in the ledger, the name, address, and resident registration number of the applicant, grounds for acquisition, period of announcement, procedures for filing objections, and other necessary matters, and shall be made in Form 21; provided, if such announcement is published in a daily newspaper, only the purpose of the announcement, the location and lot number among the description of the real estate, the period of announcement, procedures for filing objections, and other necessary matters may be specified. <Amended on Mar. 16, 1984>
  (2) Any person who has an objection to the details of a public announcement under paragraph (1) may file an objection with the competent authority in Form 22 by the date of expiration of the period of public announcement.
  (3) When the competent authority receives an objection under paragraph (2), it shall, within 2 months from the expiration date of the period of public announcement, process such objection after conducting a fact-finding investigation, and where necessary for such investigation, it may question the objector, interested persons, and other reference persons. In such cases, records of fact-finding investigations shall be compiled with the relevant documents and preserved.
  (4) A public announcement posted on the bulletin board of the offices of a Si/Gun, etc. pursuant to Article 19(3) of the Act shall be continuously posted until the expiration of the period of public announcement under that paragraph.

Article 25 (Issuance of certificates) When the competent authority issues a certificate under Article 19(3) of the Act, it shall enter such issuance in the register of issuance of certificates in Form 23.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 26 (Acquisition of unreported land as State property) The competent authority shall, with respect to land with unrestored ownership registration to be acquired as State property pursuant to Article 20 of the Act, prepare a land inventory as of the expiration date of the effective period of the Act (or, in cases under the proviso to Addenda 2 of the Act, the date of the decision or decision on re-examination by the relevant committee), and submit it to the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended on Dec. 23, 1994>

Article 27 (Remuneration for judicial scriveners) (1) The remuneration for judicial scriveners regarding registration under Article 21 of the Act shall be 50 percent of the remuneration prescribed under Article 11 of the Judicial Scriveners Act; provided, remuneration for the following services shall be free of charge: <Amended on Dec. 31, 1988>
  1. Acting on behalf of a person in filing a request for a certified copy or abstract of the register, or for various certificates related to registration (including preparation of application forms);
  2. Acting on behalf of a person in inspecting the register (including preparation of application forms);
  3. Inspection of a certified copy or abstract of the register, and preparation of applications for certificates related to registration.
  (2) Where a judicial scrivener, after commencing preparation of documents, suspends or fails to complete such work due to circumstances attributable to, or at the request of, the person who appointed him or her, he or she may receive remuneration for the documents already prepared or services already performed, within the limit not exceeding 1/2 of the remuneration under paragraph (1).

Article 28 (Retention period of documents) (1) Ledgers and documents under this Decree shall be retained for 10 years from the date on which the period for filing applications for registration or registration under Addenda 2 of the Act expires.
  (2) The register of issuance of written guarantees under Article 8(2) shall be transferred to the competent authority within 10 days from the expiration date of the effective period of the Act.
